Imphal, the 28th March , 1965. 
No. CS /2 /55 . --The following order received from the Goverument of India , 
Ministry of Food and Agriculture, New Delhi is republished for general information . 

T. Kalachand Singh , 

Asstt . Secretary to the Govt. of Manipur . 
New Dalhi, dated the 18th March , 1985 . 

ORDER 
SRO ............ In exercise of the powers conferred by sub - seotion ( 2 ) of Section 4 
of the Essential Commodities Ordinance , 1955 (Ordinance No. 1 of 1955 ), ( hereinafter 
in this Order referred to as the suid Ordinance ), the Central Government hereby makos 
the following Order , namely : 
1. Short titlo , extent and commencement : 

( i ) This Order may be called the Wheat (Removal of Movement Control) 

Order , 193.). 
( ii ) It extends to the whole of India except the State of Jammu and 

Kashmir . 

( iii ) It shall come into force on the 18th March , 1955 . 
2. Romoval of all restrictions on movement of wheat : 

As from tbe date of commencement of this Order , there shall be no prohibition , 
restriction or control on the movement of wheat froin any place in a State to any other 
place outside that State , 

3. Effect of this Order : 

This Order shall have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent therewith in 
any other enactment for the time being in force in any State to which this Order 
applies and any such enactment to the extent of inconsistency shall cease to have 
offoot at the commencement of this Order . 
4. Law made by State Governments to cease to have effect 

(n ) No order made or deemed to have been made under the said Ordinance 

by the Government of a State or by any Officer or authority in 

that State ; or 
(b ) no enactment for the time being in force in any State to which 

this Urder applies 
shall have effect 80 as to pr. ibibit , restrict or control the moveinont of wheat from 
any place in a State to any other place outside that State . 

8d /-A. Zaman , 
Joint Secretary to the Government of India .

New Delhi, the 7th February , 1955 . 
To 
The Chief Secretaries of all Part A B and O States. 

Subject : -Use of Military Ranks after 

release eto . 
Str . 

I am directed to intimate that, apart from serving officers of the Armed Foroes, 
only the following categories of persons are entitled to use military ranks with their 
námes. The recognised method of doing so is indicated below in each case : 

(a ) Regular Commissioned Officers who retire with pension or gratuity 

e.g. Captain A. ( Retd ). 
Junior Commissioned Officers granted Honorary Commissions as ICOS 

on retiremont ... ... ... ... Hony. Lt. B , ( Retd .) 
(c ) Ruling Princes granted Honorary Commissigns -Major - General C , and 

others granted Honorary Commissions- (Hony ) Major C. 
(d ) Officers of the Reserves including Emergency List of I.N. 

Capt . D , (Reserve )/ Lt. Comdr. 1 ), ( Emergency List ) / Fit . Lt. D. (Reserve) 
( o ) Officers of the Territorial Army and Officers of N.C.C.-Lt. Col. E. 

( T.A )/ Captain E , (NCC ). 
(f) Officers and others granted Foronary ranks by the Rulers of Statos 

before integration with the Union ( Hony ) Major F (with the name 

of the State in bracket ). 
2. fo order to apprise ex -officers , who held Temporary , Short Servioe , Emergency 
or any other similar type of Commission in the past , of the correct legal and official 
viow on the subject, two Press Nobes were issued by the Government of Indix on 
the 24th December, 1949 and the 6th February , 1961. They were specifically re 
quested to discontinue the use of their former military ranks in case they were doing 
80 under a misconception that it was permissible . The vast majority of ex-officers have 
complied with the advice tendered . It is noticed , however , that sometimes military ranks 
are used , where they ought not to be even in official correspondence communiques 
and press releases . It is requested that this should be avoided in all cases not covered 
by the vategories mentioned in the first paragraph and simply Shri or Mr. should 
be used . Where the use of military ránk is permitted under the first paragraph , 
the sunk used should be the substantivo rank and not any other rank . 

Yours faithfully ,

Tender Notice No. 42 . 

Imphal, the 28th March , 1965 . 
1. Sealed tenders are invited for the exclusive right to work out timber from 
the “ Uningthoupokpi Protected Forest” and will be received by the undersigned 
upto 2-0 P. M. on the 27th April, 1955. The period of contract is five years 
from the 1st May , 1955 to 30th April, 1960 . 

2. The tenderer should inspect the Forest before submission of tender to have 
a thorough , idea of the Forest which has never been worked before . The successful 
tenderer will have to construct various Forest extraction routes from the working 
depots upts the main river Iril & if required to train the rivers and 
of that area to facilitate floating down of timbers , at his own cost. The tonderer 
should indicates a proper 

aligument of the roads to be constructed and of the 
rivers to be truined showing what he contemplates to do year by year during 
the period of the lease . 

3 . The maximum annual quota of lo:98 to be extractod is limited to 600 (six 
hundred ) logs or 200 (two hundred ) trees approximately . No trees can be felled 
which is less than 6 ft , iu girth , measured at breast height i. c . 4 - 13 from tbe 
ground level. 

4. Each tenderer should state the monopoly fee in terms of pice per rupee 
of royalty on and above due royalty payable 

due royalty payable on the extracted timber , for tbe 
right of working the timber. The monopoly fee offered shall be payable each time 
with the royalty whilo taking the transit pass . The tenderer should deposit an 
earbest ironey of Rs. 100 /- (Rufees one hundred ) only in the Imphal Treasury and 
should enclose the Treasury Chalan in the tender failing which no tender will be 
accepted . The 

eargest money will be refunded in case of unsuccessful tenders 
and will be converted into a part of caution money in case of successful 

tender . 
Successful tenderer shall execute an agreement within 14 days of the receipt of 
the information to that effect and shall deposit n caution money of Rs . 200 /- (Rupees 
two hundred ) only, failing which the tender shall be treated as cancelled and the 
earnest money deposited siiall be forfeited to the Government of Manipur. On 
signing the agreement if the contractor does not do any work or if it is the 
opinion of the Forest Officer that proper extraction has not been done by the 
contractor, the agreement is liable to cancellation without further notice and the 
caution money of Rs. 200 / - only be forfeited . 
5. The boundary limits in which timbers as to be operated , are as given below : 

North : - Warilok . 
Soutb :-Ngaton -Khamson . The footpath from villager and then the 

next hill stri am which run to the north of Kharrison village 

and which juin the Ihang river. 
East ;-The Ibang River. 

West :-Foot path between Shorbung Ngaton villages. 
6. Trees which are reserved and marked for mother trees by the Forest Depart 
ment in the area stated above should not be felled . 

7. Particulars of conditions of the agreement may be seen in the Forest Office 
during Office hours . 

The undersigned does not bind himself to accept the highest tender and 
may reject any tender without assigning any reas01). 

R. K. Bijoyobandra Singh , 
Forest Officer, Government of Manipur .

1. Sealed tenders are invited for the exclusive right to work out Teak timbers 
from Burmah Border Forest " and will be received by the undersigned upto 2-0 P. M. 
on the 27th April , 1935 . The period of contruct is three years from 1st May , 1955 
to 30th April , 1958 . 

2. The tenderer should inspect the Forest before submipsion of tender to have 
· thorough idea of the Forest which has never been worked before . The maximum 
annual quots of logs to be extracted is limited to 600 logs or 200 trees approximately . 
No tree can be felled which is less than 41 ft. in girta , measured at broast height 
i. e . 4 - " from the ground level. 

8. Each tenderer shoull state the monopoly fee in terms of pioe por rupee of 
royalty on and above due royalty payable on extracted timber , for the right of working 
the timber . The monopoly fee offered shall be payable each time with the royalty 
while taking transit pass. The tonderer should deposit an earnest money of Re . 200 / 
(rapoos two hundred ) only in any Guvernmont Treasury and should enclose the Trea 
sury Chalan in the teoder failing which no tonder will be accepted . The earnest. 
money will be refunded in case of unsuccessful tenders and will be converted into a 
part of caution money in case of successful tenders. Successful tenderer shall execute 
an agreement within 14 days of the receipt of the information to that effect and shall 
deposit a . caution money of Rs. 1,000 /- ( Rupees one thauband ) only, failing which the 
tender shall be treated as oa noelled and the earnest monoy deposited shall be forfeited to the 
Governmont of Manipur. On signing the agreement if the contrastor does not do any work 
or if it is the opinion of the Forest Officer that proper extraction has not been done 
by the contraotor, the agreement is liable to cancellation without further notice and 
the caution money of Rs. 1,000 / - (Rapees one thousand) only be forfeitod . Suocess 
ful tonderer will take himself the responsibility of constructing extraction routes in 
the forests . 

4. The boundary limit in which Teak timbers are to bu operatod are as given below : 

Burmah Border Forest from Boundary Pillar No. 1 to 34 except the area covered 
by Yangoupokpi, Lokchao Reserved Forest. The extent of area wherein Teaks are to 
be oporated will approximately cover 40 sq. miles in the border lice only , 

5. Trees which are reserved and marked for mother trees by the Forest Depart 
ment in the aree stated above should not be fellod . 

6. Particulars of Qubditions of the agreemeut may be seen in the Forest Office 
during Office hours .

ject any tender without Assigning any reason ,

ভারত সরকার অনেক রেপ অগী মতুং ইন্না , হান্ন ঔজিলিয়েরি টেরিটোরিয়েল কোর্স হায়না কোন 
আই তো মহগী মা নেসলে ভােটিয়ার ফোর্স হায়বা অনা গেমগৎতে । মাসিক চহি খুদিংলা মী 
লাখ অমমমগ হিংদা আকলি চহি মঙা অসিগী মং মী লাখ মাখকঃ লানগ ট্রেনিং গনি । মাসি দক 
কেম্প ২০০ লিংখৎকনি , কেম্প খুদিংদা মী ৫০০ তম্বীগনি । ইংশােক ১৯৫। গ নে থাকা ট্রেনিং হৌগনি । তা 
হিদি : - মাইফল কাপ্পা , ফি ইঞ্জিনিয়ারিং, ফাওঁ এভ , হাইজিন, নােম যাওদা ঢিল, ফিজিকেল ট্রেনিং ,, 
ন অসিনটিবনি । 


নেসনেল ভােলন্টিয়ার ফোর্সী মতলব লান শােকননবগীদমক লাম্মী শেমগৎপা নতে ইনৈী সেবাদা পুঞ্জিং চংহ 
িইশানা ইশাৰু কৰা ভীনগমনি। মাসিদা মিং মুরগা অাইফদনা লান মাওদ দে হায়বগ অন 
করিত লৈতে । লান নত্তবা ইনবাৰী খুদোংথিৰা হায়ৰদি মুহারা , ঈশিং চাওৰগুৰা থােকল মতমদদি ইতি সেবা

No, 7 of 1968 , 

Imphal, the 29th March , 1955 . 
In exercise of the powers conferred by Section 41 of the Special Marriage Act, 
1984 ( Act 43 of 1954 ), the Judicial Commissioner , Manipur is pleased to frame the 
following rules for the purpose of carrying into effect the provisions of Chapters V , 
VI and VIL of the aforesaid Act . 
These rules shall come into force immediately . 

By Order , 
K. B. Singh , 

Registrar , 
1. In these rules unless there is anything repugnant in the subjeot or context 
* Court means the District Court as defined in sec. 2 ol, (e) of the Special Marriage 
Act, 1954 ( Act XLIII of 196+). 

“ The Act " means the Special Marriage Act, 1954 (Act XLIII of 1964 ). 

“ Prescribed " means prescribed by these rules . 
2 . An appeal filed under sec . 8 or 17 of the Act shall be accompanied by a 
certified copy of the order appealed against. As soon as an appeal is filed it shall 
be numbered according to the serial number in the prescribed register and the par 
ticulars thereof shall be entered in the same . The register shall be in Form No. 1 . 

3. The appellant shall file along with the petition of appeal or on any subsequent 
date 88 the Court may direct copy or copies of the petition and notice in the 
prescribed form for service upon the Marriage Officer and any other person who 
intervened before the Marriage Officer , who passed the order appealed against . If 
any one intervened before the Marriage Officer, the application of appeal shall state 
clearly his name and address . 

4. Notice upon the Marriago Officer will be served through post , of which the 
cost will be borne by the State , but the appellant shall file the costs for calling 
for the record , and the costs will be the same as in the case of an appeal from 
the deoree of a Civil Court of the lowest jurisdiction . Service 

upon any other 
party will be made by the process fee as is required in miscellaneous , civil appeals . 

5 . Every application under the Act whether under secs. 22, 23 , 24 , 25 , or 27 
of the Act shall be accompanied by a copy of the certificate of marriage as entered 
in the Mærringe Certificate Book . 

Book . It shall conform , as far as may be , to Form 
No. 8 and contain the particulars wentioned therein . 

6 . When the application contains a prayer for a deoree for alimony and mainte 
nance as mentioned in section 36 or 87 of the Act the wife shall file a further 
statement containing the particulars of the property of the husband which it is 


2 


MANIPDB GAZETTE , APRIL 18, 1968 . 


accompany the 


1 


sought to be charged . Such statoment should form a part of or 
petition , but may, with the loave of the Court , be filed subsequently , but before 
the application is hoard . A copy of the statement shall be supplied to the other 
side if not already furnisbed in the petition itself, and the latter may file objection , 
If any , thereto . 

9. A party filing an application under any of the aforesaid sections shall , along 
with it , file as many , copios thereof as there are parties to the proceeding, and also 
the process - fees in court fee stamps for the service thereof . The fees for service 
of these notices shall be lovied in the manner 20 mentioned in the Schedule annexed . 

8. One copy shall be served in a conspicuous part of the residence of the 
husband and wife each , and shall be in the bature of a general citation as in 
sec , 283 of the Indian Succession Act , 1925 and one oopy shall be put up on the 
potice board in the Court house for information of the general public . A notice 
in duplioate with a copy of the potition shall also be sent to the office of the 
Marriage Officer in whose office the marriage was registered for publication in his 
notice board . The Marriage Officer shall return the duplicate with his endorsement 
thereon noting that it was duly published and the date when it was so publishe i. 

9. If the parents of the applicant and Opp . Party be alive notices shall also 
be served upon them . Where there is a child of the marriage a notice shall also 
be served upon him , and if the child be a minor it shall be served in the manner 
as provided for the C. P. Code, for service of a notice upon & Ipinor defendant , 
As many notices as there are children shall be served ; but one process fee should 
be lovied if the number of children do not exceed four notwithstanding the fact 
that they may be living in separate places. Where the number exceeds four , a

particulars of any income which is not considered liable to tax for any reason 
whatsoever. If this is done, the income 80 disclosed would not be considered to 
have been concealed ovou it in the assessment it is held to be liable to tax . 

A copy of the prescribed form will be supplied free of charge to any 
person who , for the purpose of complying with this potice, applies to the Income 
tax Officer concerned . 

Every such person is further advised to ensure compliance with this notice , 
sinoe any frilure without reasonable calise to furnish the return required by this 
notioe, or failure without reasonable cause to furnish it within the time allowed 
or in the manner required will entail a penalty not exceeding one and half 
times the tax payable .

NOTIFICATION . 


Ministry of Home Affairs, 

New Delhi , dated the 26th April , 1955 . 
In exercise of the powers conferred by Section 2 of the Part C States (Laws) 
Act, 1950 (XXX of 1950 ), the Central Government hereby extends to the State of 
Manipur the Code of Criminal Procedure , 1898 (Act V of . 1898 ) , as at present in 
force in the State of Assam , with the following restrictions and modifications, 
namely_ (a ) throughout the said Code, references to the State Government shall be 
construed as references to the Chief Commissioner, (b ) in Section 1, for sub- section 
( 2), the following shall ba substituted , namely — “ (2 ) It extends to the whole of India 
except the State of Jammu and Kashmir , but in the absence of any specific pro 
vision to the contrary, nothing herein contained shall affect the Manipur State Courts 
Act , 1947 , or the Manipur State Hill Peoples ( Administration ) Regulation , 1947, or 
any order spacial or local law now in the State of Manipur, or any spacial jurist 
diction or power conferred or any special form of Procedure prescribed , by any 
other law for the time being in fvroe .” (c ) For the purpose of facilitating the 
application of the said Code in the State of Manipur, any court or other authority 
may construe the said Code with such alterations, not affecting the substance , as 
may be necessary or proper to adapt it to the matter before the court or othor 
authority . 

Sd /- A. V. Pai, 
Secretary .

It is noticed that applications for grant of Gun licenses are submitted by 
applicants from the Ilill areas , direct to the Deputy Commissioner s Office . In a 
majority of cases thoy have to be referred back to the S. D. O. concerned for re 
porting number of houses in the village , number of guns already held in 

the 
village & whether the person is considered suitable & recomended . In the mean 
while the applicants have either to wait or to return to their villages. This entails 
avoidable expenditure o : the part of the applicants . 
It is notified therefore that in future applications for Gru licenses 

Gro licenses from the 
Hill Areas will not be entertained unless submitted through the 8.9.0.5 concerned . 
S.D.0.8 will forward their reports on the application in the normal manner & will 
not hand over the applications to be applicants. 
This order will take effect from the date of publication in the official Gazette. 

V. S. Sundaram ,

India , Ministry of Home Affairs, is published for general information . : 

T. Kipgen ,

New Delhi- 2 , the 30th April , 1955 . 

RESOLUTION . 

No. 15 / 1 /55 -SST . 
In order to secure greater representation of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled 
Tribes in the public services, the maximum age - limit prescribed for appointment to 
a non -Gazetted service or post was increased by five years in the case of candidates 
belonging to theso Castes and Tribes vide Government of India , Ministry of Home 
Affairs Resolution No. 42/ 19 / 51- VGS dated the 25th June, 1952 . It has now been 
decided that this concossion should be extended to appointments to gazetted posts 
in the central Services , The applications of these orders to recruitment to All - India 
Services is separately under consideration . 

2. The above decision will take effect iinmediat: 18 . The Union Public Service 
Commission huve agreed thit where the advertisements issued by them require that 
applications from candidates should reach the Commission on a date falling within 15 
days from the date of this Resolution , the list date for the receipt of applications 
from Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe candidates will be extended by two weeks . 
Other recruiting authorities for posts under the Government of India will also 
take similar action wherever necessary . 

Sd / - G. Swaminathan , 
Joint Secy . to the Govt. of India .

In addition to the monopoly fee , royalty on canos actually extracted should 
be paid according to the Schedule rates fixed by the Assam Forest Department. Suo 

tenderers should execute an agroement within 10 days of the receipt of 
information to that effect and shall pay monopoly fee at the time of signing the 
lease failing which the tender shall be treated as cancelled and earnest inoney deposited 
will be forfeited to the State . 

The Cane Mabal of the State is divided int :) three separate Mahals as follows 
and each one should be tondered for separately .

of Jiri, Makru and Borak . 

(Mahal No. II.) 
Area comprising Blocks III, VIII, IX and X in the drainage of Borak , 
Irang and Tuijang . 

(Mahal No. III.) 
Area comprising Blocks IV , V , VI and VII in the drainage of Borak and Tuivai.

নােটিশ নং ৩ । 

তাং ১৮। ৪। ৫৫ ইং । 
১। অসিনা মরম ওইদুনা প্রজা পুষমক্তা খংহঞ্চুরি । মরমদি –মধাদা ইরিবা ফোরেষ্ট রেভিনু ষ্টেশন পুম্নমক 
অসিগী মাশুল সৌনবগী এজেন্টসিপ ( Agentship ) অসিগী থবক অসি চহি অমগীদমক হায়বদি অং ১৬৫৫ ইংদগী 
তাং ৩১৫৫৬ ইং ফাওবা তেবিনবা ফোরেষ্ট অফিস তাং ১২৫৫ ই মে ঘাগী শগােলশেল মুমিৎকী অয়ক 
পুং ১২ তাবদা করিগুম্বা টেণ্ডারা য়োনখিদ্ৰবদি নিলাম তৌছুনা মােনগনি । 

ধবক অসি তৌবিনিংবা মীশিংনা তাং ১১৫৫৫ ইংগী নুংখিল পুং ২ তাবা ফাওবা নগা মুমিৎ অসিগী 
মমাংদা রেভিনু ষ্টেশন পুদিংগী তােঙাল তােঙাল চাজুম নম্বা টেণ্ডার পিব আগনি । 

টেণ্ডাৰ পিবিরিবা মী খুদিমা টেণ্ডার খুদিংমকী লুপা ৫০, ( লুপ )ৈ আনেষ্ট মনি ( earnest 
money ) ওইনা ইস্ফাল ট্রেজরিদা থষিগদবনি অমসুং চালান কপি অমা টেণ্ডারগা লােইননা পিবিগদবনি । 

চালান 
অসি ওদবা টেণ্ডার অমতা লৌজবােই । ফাওবা টেণ্ডারগীদি আরনেই মনি অদু হন্দোকচগনি । অফাওবা টেণ্ডারগদি 
সিকুরিটি ( Security ) গ শরুক অমা ওইনা লৌবসু যাই । 

টেণ্ডারারনা মহাক্কী টেণ্ডার অদু য়ারে হায় সুমিত্তগী চয়ােন অমগী মনুংদা পাটা সহি তৌবির পাটাগী 
মতুংইন্না থবক তৌবিগদবনি । পাটা সহি তৌবা সুমিত্তা পা ১০ দগী লুপা ৫০০, ফাওবা পিবা রেভি ষ্টেসনগনা 
লুপা ৫০, (আখৈ) অমসুং লুপ ৫০০ , দগী হেনবনা সুপা ১০০ ( চামা ) ট্রেজরি চালান ওইনা জামিন ( Security) 
থগিদবনি । জামিন অসি পাঠাগী মতম ললাইগা শেলােই যাওদনা হলোকচগনি । পাটাদারনা করিগুধা সরকার 
অতােনা শেল লৈরবদি জামিন অসিদগী কক্ৰগা সরকারগী অতােন শেল অদু উশল তৌগনি , করি জামিন্দা 
তৈরি শেলন । অতােন অদু কুপখপা শুদ্ৰবদি লৌ ইঙ্খেল খাজনা তােলগা লৌখৎনা নিয়ম মতুংইল্লা সরকারগী 
শেন্দোল উশল তৌগনি । 

শ্বাইদগী শেল অহেন নব কনাগুম্বা অমগী টেণ্ডার লেবগী ক্ষমতা শ্রীযুক্ত ফোরেষ্ট আফিসারগীনি 

টেণ্ডারদা পিরিবা মমল অদুনা মতিক চাদে খল্লবদি রেভি ষ্টেশনশিং অসি তারিখ ১২৫৫৫ ইংলা ফোরেষ্ট 
অফিস নিলাম তৌদুনা মােনগনি । 
সুপা ৫০০ , ( চামঙ ) দগী হেনা রেভি ষ্টেসনগীদি কিস্তি মরিয়া থিবা য়াগনি । 

অসিৎপা শেলগ ভঙ্খাই অমা 
য়ােন সুমিতা অহানবা কিস্তি ওইনা থিরগা লেমহোবা অদুনা চপ মান্ননা কিস্তি ৩ লা লােইনা থিগদবনি । নুপা ৫০০ 
( চামা ) অমসুং অদুদগী তাবা মমলদি মােন সুমিত্ত শুনা থিবিগদবনি । 

নিলামদ । অমসুং টেণ্ডারদা শিৎপা শেলগী মথা অনৌবা সরকারগী নিয়ম মতুংইন্না শেল টেক্স (sale tax ) নুপা ১, 
দা পৈশা ২ ( অনি) গী হিংদা অমুক পিগদবনি । 

অকুপ্পা মনােল ফোরেষ্ট অফিস হবিরবা য়াগনি ।

THE ESSENTIAL COMMODITIES ORDINANCE , 1955 

No 1 of 1955 
PRUNI: I.CPATED BY TILE PRESIDENT IN TIE Firth YEW OF THE REPr BIIC OF INDIA . 
An Ordinance to provide , in the interests of the general public , for the control of 

the production , supply and distribution of, and trade and commeroe in , certain 
commodities , 

WHEREAS the Essential Supplies ( Temporary Powers ) Act, 1946 ( XXIV of 1946 ), 
which confers powers to control the production , supply and distribution of and trade 
and commerce in , certain commodities, expires on the 26th day of January , 1955 ; 

AND WUEREAs it is necessary , in the interests of the general public , to provide 
for the continuance of such powers in relation to some of the commodities specified 
in that Act and certain , other commodities ; 

AND WHEREAS Parliament is not in session and the President is satisfied that 
circumstances exist which reoder it necessary for him to take immediate action ; 

Now , THEREFORE , in exercise of the powers conferred by clause ( 1) of article 123 
of the Constitution , the Presidont is pleased to promulgate the fullowing Ordinance : 

1. Short title , extent and commencement.- ( 1) This Ordinance may be called 
the Essential Commodities Ordinance , ! 955 . 

( 2 ) It extends to the whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir . 
( 3 ) It shall come into force on the 26th day of January , 1955 . 
2. Definitions.-- In this Ordinance, unless the context otherwise requires , - 
( a ) " essential commodity ” means any of the following classes of commodities 

( ) coal, including coke and otber derivatives ; 
(ii ) component parts and accessories of automobiles ; 
( iii) cotton and woollen textiles ; 
(iv ) iron and steel, including manufactured products of iron and steel ; 
(v ) paper , including newsprint, paper board and straw board ; 
( vi) petroleum and petroleum products ; 
(vii) falt ; 
(viżi) sugar ;

being a commodity with resp.:ct to which Parliament has power to make laws by 
virtue of entry 33 in List lll in the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution ; 

(6 ) " notified oriler” moins un order notified in the Official Gazette ; 
( c ) 

- State Government” in relation to y part C state means the Lioutenant 
Governor or the Chief Commissioner, as the case may be.

PRESS NOTE . 
In accordance with the interpretation of Article 280(1) (a) of the Constitution of India 
Liven by the Supreme Court in their judgment dated 30th Marclı, 1953 in A case regarding 
the Bombay State versus the United Motors and others , sales tax is leviable on non -resident 
dealers ly the State in which yoods sold by them are delivered for consumption . This 
State Government have , therefore , decided to lovy sales tax on all such sales affected on or 
after the 1st January , 1954. 

It is further notified for the information of non - resident deal.rs that the taxable quan 
tum iu their case has been prescribed at Rs.5,000 and the dealers who are liable to pay tax 
should , before 15th February, 1955 , apply to the Excise & Taxation Officer, Non - reridents 
Circle , Patiala , for registration under section 7 of the PEPSU General Sales Tax Ordiance , 
2006 , along with a treasury receipt of Rs. 5 as registration fee to be deponited in the Govt. 
treasury at Patiala . The registration fee can also be remitteil by a Bank Draft on the 
Imperial Bank of Indir at Aubala , Delhi and Bombay drawn in favour of the Treasury 
Officer, l’atiala , which should be forwurdod t ) the aforesaid assessing authority . 

The non -resident registered dealers shall submit by post quarterly returus within 30 
days of the quarter ending 30th June , 30th September , 318t December and 31st March 
every year in the prescribed form , obtaioable free from the said assessing authority , in 
respect of sales made for consumption in this state, along with the amount of tax payable 
in the manner alrendy stated above. The declaration forma prescribed for the purpose and 
duly signed by the purchasing registered dealers , shall also be fornished along with the 
quarterly returns . 

It has been further arranged that the accounts of a dealer would be examined at 
centrally located place in his State and efforts would be made to hear appeals in the 
dewler s State of residence . 

In PEPSU , there is a single point sales tax and the tax is chargeablo at the rate of 
two pice a rupee subject to deduction , laid down in sections and 6 of the said Ordinance . 

Copios of the Sales Tax Ordinance and the Rules thereunder can bo had from the 
Superintendent, Bhupendra State Press, Patiala , on payment .

অমা অমসুং তা : ৪৫৬ ইদগা তাং ৩১৩৫৭ ইং ফাওবা অগিগ রেট ( rate ) অমা ভােঙান , তােঙামা মম 
নিসিগী উৎপাদৰনি । 

টেণ্ডর পৰীনিংবা মী খুদিমকা অনেষ্ট ( e৫ // ex ) মনি ( mdme ) ওইনা লুপ ৫০, ইম্ফাল ট্রেঞ্জরিদা 
( Impokut Tre » ura ) দা গম্বীগদবনি অমস্ত চালান কপি জমা টেণ্ডরগা লােইননা পিবিগবনি । Bato (chalan ) 
মাওবা টেণ্ডর অমতা লৌজরােই । 

টেলগীদি আরনেষ্ট মনি অদু হলােকচগনি । অফাওবা টেণ্ডগীদি 
আরনেষ্ট মনি অদু সেকিউরিটি (secutta ) গী শৰুক অমা ওইনা পাটার্গী মতম লােইদ্রিবা ফাঙৰ গম্ব নাই । 
টেরারনা মহাকী টের অদু য়ারে হায়বা চয়ােল অমগী মংদা পাই। সহি তেবিলগা পাট্টা 

পাট্টা মতুংইমা 
এক তৌৰিগৰনি । পাটা সহি তৌবা সুমিত্তা মােননাপােলি ফী অপু পিগদবনি অমসুং সুংফম অসিগী মােনােপােলি 
ফি অদুনা লুপা চাম্মদগী চামঙা ফাওবা ওইরগা লুপ ৫০ , ( য়া )ৈ , সুপা ৫০০ ( চামঙ) ) দী হেনলগা লুপ। ১০০ , 
( চা ) ট্রেজারি চালান ওইনা জামীন ( security ) খন্বিগবনি । জামীন অসি পাটাগী মতম লােইরগা শেলাই 
মাওদন হলোকচগনি । পটাদারন । কবিগু সরকারগী অতােন শেল লৈরবদি জামীন অসিদগী ককলগা অতােনবা শেল অদু 
উশল ভোগনি । করিও জামিন অসিনা অতােনা অনু কুপখৎপা শুদ্ৰবদি লৌ ইঙ্গেল খাজনা তােগা লোখৎপা নিয়ম মতুংইয়া 
সরকারগী শেলােল উশােল তৌগনি । 

কুংফম অসি শুবিনিংবা নীশিংনা টেণ্ডর তৌদ্রিঙৈদা হান্না মফম অদু চতুনা য়েংবিৰুৱগা দে ওর তৌবিগদবনি । 
লৌবা মতুংদা মুংফম মুং লৈমদ্রে শেল হনবীয় হায়বনচিংবা তৌরকপা দাবী অমৎতা লৌজরােই । পাটাগী মতম 
লােইর মতুংদা সুংফমদা ইক্তবা মুং থন আরেই । থন থােক্লবদি সরকারগী ওইগনি । 

৬ । সুং শুবা মতমদা ফুকলি সুং অদু লােইদ্রিঙৈদা অতােপ্পা কুংফম অমা মচেৎ, মচেৎ ওইনা শুবা আমােই । 
Tং ইবা শিং মানব মতমদা পাকনা শিং মানবা মায়েই । জাৎ খাইবা উগ জাং ওই ককপা মারোই 
উ মচা ফুৎ অমন কোনবা উদগী হেন ভাক্তা য়ানগদবনি । ফোরেষ্ট ডিপার্টমেন্টনা মরুগীদমক খাকপা উ য়ানবা মারােই । 
৭। ক্বাইদগী শেল হেনব নব কনাগু অমগী টেণ্ডর লৌবগী ক্ষমতা যুক্ত ফোরেষ্ট অফিসারগনি । 

মােনগদ মুংফমগী মমিং । 
হৈরাংগােইলােক শু নুংফম ।

লােক তুরেলগী মরু -বাইদা লৈা শুনু নুংফম শৌবােম অমসুং কাংখল যানবী শুধু মুফমগী মাইল অহুম অমসুং ৩২ 
নােম লাপননা শৈবা শু পুংফমনি ।

Imphal, the 31st May , 1955 . 
No. CS / 3 / 55.- In exercise of the powers conferred by Section 3 of the Essential 
Commodities Act, 1955 (10 of 1955 ) and with the previous concurrence of tbe Central 
Government, the Chief Commissioner of Manipur is pleased to make the following Order : 

Manipur Foodgrains (Movement) Control Order , 1955 . 
1. Short title , commencement and application . 

(a ) This Order may be called the " Manipur Foodgrains (Movement) Control 

Order , 1955. 

(b ) It shall come into force forthwith and extend to the whole of Manipur . 
2. Definitions . 
( 1) " Foodgrains” for the purpose of this order means “ Rice , paddy and produets" 

thereof. 
(2) " Rice and paddy products " inolude Chira , Muri, Khoi, Broken rice and 

any article whatsoever which originally comes from paddy excepting husk 
and bbusi. 


2

4 . 


3. (a ) No person shall export or attempt to export any Foodgrains from Manipur 
to any place outside Manipur, except under and in accordance with a permit issued 
by the State Government or any officer authorised by the State Government in 
this behalf . 

(6 ) No person shall transport , attempt to transport, cause to be transported 
or offer for transport any Foodgrains into the urea of the State lying to the north 
of the village Kangpukpi except under and in accordance with a permit issued by 
the State Government in this behalf.

APPEALS AN :) APPLICATIONS . 
Rules framed under Art 227 of the constitution of India road with section 6 (b ) of the 
Judicial Commissionmi s Courts ( Declaration as lliglı Courts ) Act 1950. Thoy shall come 
in force with immedizte effect . 

1. ( 1 ) Every memoranduin of appeals or objection and every application shall 
bear the general huadin : - 

“ In the court of the Judicial Commissoiner , Manipur , Imphal. 
( 2 ) Fevery nemorandum of Appeal or () bjection or Application for Review 

or Revision shall immediately below the title , have endorsed on it 
• First Appeal " Seco : d Appeal ” , Appol frum Order or “ Revision " 

or " Application for Review " as the case may be and shall state . 
( 1 ) The names father s name and in the case « f a female husband s name 

and full postal address of each appellaut or application ; 
( 2 ) The nam : father s name and in the case of female husband s naine and 

full postal address of each Respondent . 
2. Every memorandum of Appeal or Objection and every application shall be 
in the language of the court and shall set out oncisely in numbered paragraphs 
the facts upon which the applicant relies and the ground upon which the court is 
asked to grant the relief and shall conclude with a prayer stating clearly as far as 
circumstances permits the exact nature of the relief sought . 

3. Every application made in pending case shall state the section and the Act

GOVERNMENT OF

The Govt . of India havo decided to award in 19955-50 , 30 scholurships tenable 
abronit to Indian natic nals for specialising in Arabic , Chinese , French , German , 
Italian , Japanese , Persian , Spanish , Turkish and Russian . 

Only candidates sponsored and recommended by the Universities / comparable insti 
tutions/Central or State Govts . whu pre prepared to serve the sponsoring authorities 
for at least thrra ye:urs after their return 10 India will be considereit . They should 
have a good University degree and except for awards in Spanish , Italian , Turkis ) 
and Japanese languages, should have already studied the language concerned and 
acquired proficiency therein . Candidates for Scholarships in Spanish , Italian , Turkish , 
and Japanese languages should have clem : ntary knowledy, or aptitude for 

the 
foreign language concerned . Candidates should not be 

than forty years

nance and cost of travel .

soring Authorities or from the Government of India , Ministry of Education , Scholar 
ships and Information Division ( coction S. 1 ), New Delhi. The last date for the

The Government of India have provided y sum of Rs. 1,30,00,000;- for the 
year 1955-56 to award scholarships to scheduled Castes , Scheduled Tribes and other 
Backward Classes . The scholarships are tenable in recognised lostitutions . in India 
imparting education beyond the Matri ulation stage in the following courses 
tioned in order of preforonce . 

( a ) Medicine and allied subjects including Nursing . 
(b ) Engineering and Architecture. 
(c ) Agriculture, Forestry and Veterinary Science . 
(d ) Technology . 
( e ) Science . 
(f ) Education and Social Service . 
(g ) Humanities ( including Arts), Social Science , Fine Arts and Languages . 
( b ) Commerce . 

( i) Law and Library Science . 
The last date of receiving applicatiuns by the Ministry of Education , New Delhi 
is 31st July , 1955. Particulars of the amount of scholarships, instruction to candi 
dates, regulations and application forms may be obtained in the Offices of the 
Superintendent (Home Office ), the Sub-divisional Officers , the Principal, D. M. College ,

Subject : 

CAR FESTIVALS OF 1955 . 
The Car festivals of Lord Jaganath at Puri will be celebrated from the 5th of 
June, 1955 and will continue till the 4th of July , 1955 . This festival, as usual, 
will attract large numbers of pilgrims from all 

India . It is observed that 
epidemics of cholera break out . either during or after the festival: de sporadic 
Cuses of cholera are being reported froin some parts of Orissa and also from neighbouring 
States, particularly from bordering States , it is felt that the intending pilgrims 
should be advised through newspapers and other sources to get themselves protected 
against cholera sufficiently in advance . 

Adequate medical and public bealth arrangements are being undertaken in this 
State on the occasion but as mentioned before, it is desirable that the pilgrims 
intending to visit Puri from your State should get themselves inocula ! ed and obtain 
necessary inoculation certificate, as otherwise they will not be allowed to enter into 
the festival areas without such inoculation certifioite . Temporary regulations making 
cholera inoculation compulsory in the festival area under the Epidemic Diseases Act , 
1897 from 15th of April 1955 to 15th July , 1955 are being enforced . 

enf orced . Holi ers of 
certificates of inoculation issued after 1-4-55 will however not be required to take 
furtber inoculation in the festital area .

নিলাম নােটিশ নং ৪ । 


তাং ২৪।৫।৫৫ ইং । 


মরমদি : 


অসিনা পাৎকী পাটাদারশিং অমসুং মনিপুরগী প্রজা পুমা খঙহন্নি । 

মখাদা ইরি পাৎকী পাটাদানশিং মখােই মখােইনা তাং ১৫৫৫৫ ইং ফাণ্ডবদা খীফম থােকপা অহান 
কিন্তী থীরদৰা নগা শুনা থাদবগীদমক লেমহৌরিবা মতম , তাং ৩১৩৫৬ ইং ফাওবা চান পাশিং অসি তাং ২৮৬৫৫ 
ইং লৈপাপােকপা দুমিৎকী অমুক পুং ১১ তাবদগী হোন ডিপুটি কমিশনার আফিসদা মখাগী করারশিং অসিগী মতুংইয়া 
অমুকহ নিলাম তোদু মােনগনি । 

( ক ) নিলাম ওকপিরবা মীনা নিলাম মফমদা আমদ্ৰবদা ওকলিবা পাৎলগী সিকুরিটি ( জামিন ) গা অহানা কিস্তি , 
পাংমলগী শরুক , গা পুন্না খাবিগবনি ; শােয়রগা খুদা পাৎ অপু অমুক হন্না নিলাম তৌদুনা মােনগনি । অকোনবা নিলাম 
অসিদা পাংমল হরদি হস্থরিবা শেল অদু হান্না নিলাম ওকপা মীনা হাপকৎকবনি । 

( খ) নিলাম ওকপা মুমিৎ ৭ নিগী মনুদা সিকুরািগী শরুক অদু পাংমলগী শরুক ! শুনবা হাপকৎকদৰনি । অরেই 
কিস্তিনা তাং ৩১৭৫৫ ইং ফাওবা খীগদবনি । শােইরবদি হাগা থাখিবা শেল পুম্নমক মলগা পাৎ অমুক হন্না নিলাম 
তোবা যাই । 

( গ ) নিম তেলিবা আফিসারনা খাইদগী চাওবা দাগ নগা করি গুম্বা দাগ অ লৌদবসু য়াই : অদুগা পাৎশেল 
থীরর পাৎ অছু নিলাম পুখােবসু য়াই । 

(ঘ) নিলাম অসি আবগী অকোইবা হুকুমদি চীফ কমিশনারনা লেপকনি । 


R. C. Chaulbury . 
Deputy Cominissioner, Manipur .

Dated Shillong , the 3rd June , 1955 . 
No. TM / 10 /55 /8. - Consequent on the separation of accounts from audit in respect 
of Food , Rehabilitation and Supply Departments of the Government of India all payments 
relating to the Food , Rehabilitation and Supply Miuistries of the Goveromunt of 
India from April , 1955 (Payable in May 35 ) onwards will be made by the Soparated Pay 
and Accounts Offices by Bank Drafts. Receipts relating to these Departments will 
however, continue to be credited at the treasuries as before and such credits will 
be passed on to the Pay and Accounts Officers by this office weekly by means of 
Bank Drafts . 

In Order, therefore , to enable this office to settle the transactions on account 
of Food , Rehabilitation and Supply Ministries weekly with the Pay and Accounts 
Officer concerned the Treasury Officers in Assam , Tripura and Manipur are hereby 
requested to furnish this office with a statement showing the transactions relating 
to these ministries arising at their treasuries in Form T. A. 47 on the 8th , 18th 
24th and the last day of each month accurding to the provisions of Art 117 of 
the Account Code , vol. II. 

S. N. Bhuyan , 
Assistant Accountants Officer , Assam .

অসিনা মম ওইদুনা প্রজা পুমা খংহঞ্জরি । 

পুমা খংহৰি । মরমদি - কনাগুনা সুহেং-খােলদাংবদা গাের্ণমেকী শান্ত 
ৰাইৰীগে হায়বদি মখাগী নিয়মশিং অসিথ মইনা থৰক তৌবীগদবনি । 

১। শামু অৱাইমন - এর নাে কানা শিজিন ওইগা নুপা ৩০ , ( ক ) অনুগা বরগ অনিল 
খিজির হায়বদি চংখিবদা বর তােলগা হল্লকপদা কন্যা তােংলবদি সুপ ৪০ (নিফু ) অসি শিদিগদ হপ্তা অ 
কালিলৈ অকিন্ত মতম চানা লাক্তন মথ হায়রি রেট ম ই অইমন থিৰিগদৰনি । 

২। শামু লাকপা মতমদা ফৌ লিখায় অমা , সকু মঙা, মউ কপা মতম শােয়দ পিবিগবনি । 
৩। করিও নােং - চি দুনা শামু হন খুদো চাদি মউৎকী চান -থবা পিৰীগৰনি । 

৪। শামু বাইরম্নগা কৰিগুৰা যুম- কৈ মাংদুনা মৈথােকপা ভাবদি খুদা ( অফি ) বিপাের্ট পিৰীগৰনি । 
মৈধ্যে লুমিং অদুদা শামু শংভবদি পৈশা হঞ্জরাই । 

শান্তনা , বাইরিবা মফম আর গৌরগা , করিগুনা মরম আমদী শিজিদ তাৱৰদি , পার্টিন গােভর্ণমেন 
পিবি অাইমন অদু অমুক হঞ্জনােই ।

Imphal, the 25th June , 1955 . 
The following notification is published for general information : 

T. Kipgen , 

Secretary to the Government of Manipur . 
GENERAL CONDITIONS OF GRANT- IN - AID . 
1. Every Aided Schcol must be conducted in accordance with the Rules and 
Orders of the Education Department 

2 . The curricula , as notified from time to time by the Education Department, 
must be followed and text books selected from the list of approved text books, 

3. The appointment, confirmation and dismissal of teachers must be approved , 
in the case of High Schools by the Inspector of Schools , and in the case of schools 
of lower grade by the Deputy Inspector of Schools . 

In the latter case an appeal may be made to the Inspector of Schools whose 
decision shall be final. 

No building operations must be undertaken until the plans and estimates 
have been approved by the Department . 

5 . All receipts and disbursements must be entered in the account books of the 
school which shall be open to examination by any authorised officer and copy 
of the audited accounts shouid be submitted annually to the Inspector of Schools. 

6. Grants will be paid inonthly on the basis of a statement in prescribed 
form which shall be submitted by the school authority at the close of each month 
to the Inspector of Schools in the case of High Schools and schools enjoying 
special grants, to the Deputy Tospector in the case of Middle and Primary Schools . 

7. Grants are payable on bills drawn by the School authority in the preecribed 
form and countersigned by the Inspector of Schools in the case of High and special 
schools and by the Deputy Inspector of Schools in the case of Middle and Primary 
Schools . 

8. Surplus funds shall be placed in the Post Office Savings Bank or otherwise 
as approved by the Inspector of Schools . 

No part of the surplus fund shall be spent without the sanction of the Inspector 
of Schools except for payment of the sanctioned staff . 

9. Goveroinent may claim a fair share of any balance at the credit of an aided 
school on its abolition as well as of the sale proceeds of any building , furniture or 
other property for which a grant may have been made . 

10 . The rate of pay fixed by a school, for its teaching staff must receive the 
approval of the countersigning authority . 

11 . The percentage of students passing the Matriculation Examination of a particular 
High School should not fall below prescribed minimum percentage for three consecutive 
years . 

12 . No teacher of an aided Institution shall take part in party or other politics . 
Participation in politics shall include : 

(a ) Holding an office, paid or honorary, in party organisation including 

membersbip of the Executive Committee . 
( b ) Addressing political meetings. 
( c ) Conduoting election campaigas . 

(d ) Taking part in strikes, demonstrations and the like. 
13. Discipline should be properly maintained in the sobcol. 

14. Grant - in -aid will be liable to be withdrawo for broach of any of the above . 
oonditions.

No. C -HDE / 102 / 53 / 120. - The Chief Commissioner is pleased to make the follo 
wing rules for tbe award of High School scholarships in Manipur : 

Rules for the award of High School scholarships in Manipur . 
(1 ) Every year on the result of Middle School competitive examination , 11 
(eleven ) sobolarships of the valuo of Rs. 7 ( Rupees seven ) each per month payable 
for 12 months in each year will be awarded of which 6 ( six ) will be for opeu 
compotition , 2 (two) reserved for girl students and 3 (three) for 

students and 3 (three ) for tribal students . 
(2 ) The scholarships will be tennble for 4 (four ) years in any recognised High 
School subject to good conduct and progress. 

( 3 ) Candidates must not be over 16 (sixteen ) years of age. 

(4 ) The Chief Commissioner will be the authority to grant or withdraw the 
scholarship . 

( 5 ) In any particular year if there is no suitablo candidate to wlioin a reserved 
scholarship can be awarded the Chief Commissioner may give the available schular 
ship to any other deserving candidate . 

(6 ) . The results of the scholarship -holders in each terminal Examination should 
be intimated to the Inspector of Schools by the Head Masters of the High Sobools 
concerned along with reports on their attendance ; the scholarship may be withdrawn 
by the Chief Commissioner on the grounds of inadequate progress of the holders 
or their misconduct , and the decision of the Chief Commissioner shall be final

No. C.HDE / 5 /53. -The following document is published for general infirmation . 

T. Kipgen ,

(Ministry of Education ) 

( clolarships and Information Division ) 
Sub .-- Particulars regarding a scholarship offered to an Indian national by the Government 

of Switzerland . 

1 . The Government of Switzerland have offered one scholarship for a period 
of one year during 1955.56 to an Indian national for higher Study /Research / in any 
branch of Science / Technology /Engineering at any of the Swiss Universities, research 
establishments or similar Institutions of higher learning. 
2. Other terms and conditions . 

( i ) The amount of scholarship is 500-700 Swiss Frances ( France - 1.089 

Rupees ) p.m. the amount will be fixed by the Swiss Government 
according to the academic standard of the candidate and the pro 

gramme for his studies . 
( ii ) Exemption from tuition fees . 
( iii ) The cost of tourist class Ses passage expenses from India to Switzer 

land and back. will be provided by the Govt. of India . 
( iv ) Selection candidate is expected to reach Switzerland in the beginning 

of October , 1935 . 
3. Tuose possessing Master s degree in Science or a degree or equivalent qualification 
in Engineering / Technology from a recognised university are eligible to apply . Candidates 
above 35 years of age on 1st August, 1955 will not be considered . 

4 . Preference will be given to the candidates knowing German or French language . 
While selecting the candidate , such personal attributes as make him /her especially 
fit for furtherance of international understandiog would be considered as necessary 
qualifications . 

5 , The candidates are required to send the fullowing documents along with 
their applications : 

( i ) Two pass - port size photographs with the signature of the candidate 

on the reverse . 
( ii ) Attested copies of certificatos /diplomus /degrees in respect of the 

qualification claimed ( not returnable ) . 
( iii ) Detailed programme of study which the candidate intends to under 

take in Switzerland . 
( iv ) The curriculum of studies already completed . 
( v ) Health certificate from a Registered Medical Practitioner that the 

candidate is of sound physical constitution . 
Prescribed appliontion forms eto . can be had from the Ministry of Education 
( Scbolarships and Information Division ) Section S - 1 New Delbi. The last date for 
the receipt of applications in the Ministry of Education is 20th July , 1958 . No 
application will be considered without a fee of Rs. 5 ( Rs. 1 / 4 /- in the case of 
Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes ) which should be sent 
through the postal order along with application in favour of the Ministry of Education , 
Govt. of India, New Delhi. Amount remitted through money order or cheque will 
not be accepted . 

Applications received after the prescribed date will not be given any consideration .

logy 1950-56 . 
The Government of India have received an offer of a Fellowship from Unesco to 
enable an Indian national to take up study in the field of Educational Psychology 
at the International Institute of Child Study, Bangkok , Thailand for a period of 12 
months in 1955-56 . 

Candidates should possess at least an M. A. or M. Sc . degree in education , edu 
cational Psychology , cultural anthropology , sociology , social work or psychology , and 
at least five years practical experience in education as teacher , head master training 
college lecturer or in such technical aspects of administration as curriculum planning 
of educational guidance . Only those candidates who possess the above qualifications - 
and are sponsored and recommende:1 by Universities / Comparable institutions/ Central or 
State Governments with guarantee of re-employment will be considered . Full parti 
culars and prescribed application form may be obtained from the above authorities 
of the Ministry of Education , Government of India , Scholarships and Information 
Division ( Section S - 1 ) to whom applications should be forwarded through the sponsoring 
authorities so as to roach on or before the 15th July , 1965 after which dute na 
applioations will be ontertained .

Subjeot :-Extension of date for sen ding Adtice for Inter-Government Adjustments 

to the Central Accounts Section of the Reserve Bank of India . 
It is notified for information of all Treasury Officers and Sub - Treasury Officers 
and Departmental Disbursing Officers that all cash and bouk transactions involving 
inter -Governmental adjustments that originate towards the close of the year should 
be advised by the A. G. to the Central Accounts Section of the Reserve Bank 
of India by the 15th April as required under Article 88 of the Account Code 
Vol. IV . But it has been observed that this due date could not be adhered to 
during last several years due to non -receipt of the returns from the Treasury and 
Departmental Disbursing Officers by the A. G. timely . 

All Treasury Officers and Departmental Disbursing Officers are , therefore , 
quested to tako special steps to submit all returbs of inter -Governmental transac 
tion in advance so as to enable the A. G. to settle the transaction with the Rosarve 
Bank of India by the due date .

PRESS NOTE . 
INVITATION OF COMPENSATION APPLICATIONS 

Last date for filing September 26 , 1955 . 
The Central Government have published a notification in the Gazette of India 
dated June 27 , 1955 under Section 4 of the Displaced Persons ( Compensation and 
Rehabilitatiou ) Act, 1954 inviting applications for compensation from all those dis 
placed persons with verified claims for immovable property left in West Pakistan , 
who have not applied before under any of the priority categories or otherwise . 

Applications for compensation should be preferred ia duplicate on the prescribed 
forn and handed over or sent to the Settlement Ollicer within whose juridiction 
the applicant resides , or carries on business or works for gain . The prescribed forms 

on sale at all Settlement OfBces under the Central Ministry of Rehabilitation , 
and at Post Offices . In addition to the various documents which form part of the 
applications, overy claimant should put in an aflidavit in the form specificd under 
the rules and attested by a Magistrate or an Oaths Commissioner or by any other 
officer competent to administer an oath , and sh uld also send three passport size 
photograpbs and a certified copy of tho claim assessment order . Applicants are 
quired to give full details of loans , etc. owing from them as also arrears of rent . 
Under the rules , severe penalties aro prescribed for falso information given in regard 
to these public dues. 

Those claimants who have already sent in their applications for compensation in 
the priority categories or in connection with the purchase of property , or the gran 
tiny of loans, or otherwise , need not apply again . 

In those cases where the original claimint bas died and successors in interest 
now wish to put in applications for compensation , they should , in addition to the 
documents comprising the application form , als , submit particulars of the date and 
place of death of the deceased clumant with a duly certified death certificate and 
give particulars of heil s and relatives of the deceased and a trua copy of the will 
or other document on which they rely . Such successors in interest will also have 
to swear an affidavit in support of their stateinents. 

R. F. A. lounees should obtain a certificate from the Rehabilitation Finance Admi 
nistration regarding the total amount duo from them as principal and interest as 
on June 30 , 1955 , and send this certificate along with their compeosation applications. 

Applicants should fill in all the particulars required in the forms carefully so 
as to avoid delay which will be caused iſ inaccurate or incomplete information is given . 
The last date for the filing of compensation applications is September 26 , 1955. 

A list of Settlement Officers all over India with their rerpective jurisdictions is 
given below for the guidance of applicants . 

Displacrd persons with verified claims residing outside India , who have not already 
applied , should apply to the Regional Settlement Commissiuner , Khan Murket , New 
Delhi, either directly or through a duly appointed agent or through the uccredited 
Missions abroad . 

For full details of the procedure to be followed , applicants may refer to the rules 
under the Displaced persons (Componsation and Rehabilitation ) Act , which have been 
published in the Gazette of India . 
Ministry of Rehabilitation 
New Delbi, June 26 , 1953 .

No. 24 ( 2 )/54 - Adm . In view of the importance of expedition and 

expedition and economy in 
the execution of river valley projects , the Government of India have arranged to 
bold Engineers Seminars periodically to enable the heads of major projects to make 
suggestions for improving the methods of work and efficiency and exchange views 
on technical and administrative matters common to these projects and take, wherever 
necessary , co -ordinated action . To derive the maximum benefit from suggestions 
designed to ensure economy and expedition it is important that there should be 
no avuidable delay in taking follow up action . This can not be done unless deci 
sions are taken quickly at the highest level and the suggestions implemonted both 
by the Central and the State Governments . The Government of India have , thero 
fore , set up , in consultation with the State Governments concerned , " the Co -ordi 
nation Committee of Engineers” and “ the Co - ordination Board of Ministers” . The 
composition of the Committee and the Board is as follows :

1. Candidates for the award of Scholarships shall be inembers of the Scheduled

any other equivalent examination of a recognised

the District Board /Gazetted Officer stating that he/ she belongs to Scboduled Castes / 
Sobodulod Tribos /Other Backward Classes, and is a citizen of India .

14. The scholarship shall ordinarily he tenable for a period not exceeding one 
academic year it may be renewed at the discretion of the Board subject to funds 
being available for a period not exceeding one academic year at a time to enable 
the holder to complete an approved course of study . 

16. If a scholar fails to pass the annual examination for the course of study 
for which scholarship is awarded in a year, the scholarship will automatically cease 
and his scholarship will ordinarily be renewed . He may , however, apply for a fresh 
scholarship again after passing the annual examination in future year . If & scholar 
is unable to appear in the annual examination owing to illness, he should inform 
the Board accordingly before the examination is over through the Head of the 
Institution with a medical certificate from registered medical practitioner ; failing 
which his application for renewal of scholarship will not be considered . The application 
for renewal will be considered only if the Head of the Institution , on the basis of 
performance , certifies that the candidate was likely to pass if he had taken the 
Examination . 

16. A scholarship shall be cancelled if the scholar changes the subjeot of course 
for which the scholarship was originally awarded or changes the Institution of study , 
WITHOUT THE PRIOR APPROVAL OF THE BOARD . The Heads of Institu 
tions shall report such cases to the Board and stop payment of scholarship money . 
The amount already paid may also be recovered at the discretion of the 

the Board . 
17 A scholar is liable to refund the scholarship amount at the discretion of 
the Board if be discontinues his studies during the course of the year for which 
& scholarship is awarded .

act or

through the Head of the Institution to the Board as soon as the period covered 
by euch instalment is over , otherwise the payment of the 2nd instalment will be

ইম্ফালদা নেশনেল ভােলুনটিয়ার ফোর্শ কেশ 


ইমাল, তাং ২৮।৭।৫৫ ইং জুলাই । 
মনিপুরদা নেশনে ভােটিয়ার কেম্প ভাং ১৫ সেপ্তেদশ খুলিগনি মানু অং ১৪ ওরে ১৯৪৫ দ 
লােগনি । নেশনেল ভােলুটিয়ার ফোর্স হায়বা অলি লানগদমক্তা লৈবাক কিনবা নত্তে , মসিগী মরু ওই রাখলদি 
দেশ বাশি দিংমক জাতিগ ওইনা খাং কনবা , লমচৎ ব্যবহার ফজ অমসুং দেশগ সেবাদা পুচিংবা অনননি । 

মুমিৎ ৩০ নিগ ট্রেনিং অসি , চহি ৫ গ মনুদা মী লাখ মাদা পীগনি, ভারতকী মফম খুদিং নে ১ লাদগী 
কেশ ২০০ লিংদুনা মী লাখ অমা ট্রেনিং গদবনি । ট্রেনিং টিম খুদিংমক কেপতেন অমলা ওফিসার কলিং 
ওইগনি । 

ত্রেনিং চংৰা য়া -য়াদ অমসুং শ্রেনি অমন তৌগদ মরমশিং 
চহি ১৮ দগী ৪০ ফাওবগী মনুদা লৈ মশা ফব ভারতকী নাগরিক সুদিংমক চংবা গনি । সিফাই খ 
অসং এন, সি , সি , কেডেত ওইরিবশিদি গাওবা , মারােই । 

মশানা য়ানা ট্রেনিং ভৌগদৌরিবা মী খুদিংমক অরেঙ্গা নাইদনা কুমিৎ ৩০ নিগী ট্রেনিং নপুং ফানা য়াওগদবনি , ট্রেনিং 
লৈরিঙৈদা করিগু মিলিটারি এক্ত অমত্তগী মখাপােন নত্তে, লােইরগ মিলিটারি সাতিশ চংগদখনি হায় করি 
তা লৈতে । 

ট্রেনিশিংনা ট্রেনিংদা লৈরিঙৈদা শােক - পন , লাইনা পকপকপা অমসুং শিবা থােকসবদি সরকার মানুপ দায়ি 
লৌহুনা পেলন নগা করিগু মখলগ ক্ষতি পুরন পররাই । 

কনাগু ট্রেনি অমৰু , মরম চানা , কেম্পতগী , তাহােকপা , মাগী পােকেট এলায়েন্স ককথৎপনচিংবাওফিশর 
কলিং তৌবা মই । ট্রেনিশিংগীদমক তমুর খন কেম্প লৈফম ফংগনি । 

জেনিঙদা লৈরিঙৈদা ত্রেনিশিঙনা ফংগদ অমসুং অতৈ অকুপ- অ ” 
ট্রেনিশিংনা কেম্প লৈরিঙৈদা শিজিক্সবা কেম্পকী পােৎ খুদিংমক ট্রেনিং লােইরগা অমুক লৌশিনহেগনি। 

বেশনঃ - ট্রেনিংদা লৈরি মী খুদিংমক ফ্রি রেশন ফংগনি নগা নােমদা ট্রেনি অমল রেশন এলাওয়েল ওই 
সুপা ১০ ( শিকি মঙ ) ফংগনি । হায়রি এলাওয়েল অলি রেশন সপ্লাই তৌবা ঙমবা মতমতনি । 

তলৰ অমসুং এলায়েন্স ট্রেনিং মপুঃ ফারবা মতুংদা মী অমন নোংমদা মখাই ১ গী ( ০ ) হিংসা 
মিৎ ৩০ নিগ সুপা ১০ পােকেট খচ্চা ফংগনি । 

অৱা পােগ্রামঃ- ট্রেনিং টিম খুদিংশ অৱ -পােৰানব মরমদা লুপা ৩০০, কাইথথাকলি, মাসিনা ট্রেনিশিংগী 
পুনিং শৌগৎনবা অফ মাইকৈদা শেমগৎ শাগৎপগী ওইনা — পাননবা নুঙাইবা ইরিক লাইশু, থামফোন রেকোর্ড ভাবা , 
ইশ-নােমাইগী যন্ত্র খােবা , মখল মখলগ শায়বা অসিনচিংবা অসিঙ্গ দমা চাদিং তৌগনি । 

অকুপ অতঃ —ইনামেল্লড মগ, মেস তিন , মখল মখলগ খাকি কুরিৎ অমসুং খােএাও, তুপ, চেপালি, বেগ ,

DRAFT ANNOUNCEMENT 
The Central Social Welfare Board will consider enrly in November applications 
for grants from voluntary institutions for the period November, 1955 to March , 1956 . 
Institutions may send in their applications to this office immediately in any case not 
later than 20th Angust , 19.35 on tby prescribed proforma, copies of which can be 
obtained from this office . The original copy with a copy should be sent to this office 
and another advance copy to the Central Social Welfare Buard , 10 -- Kitchner Road , 
Diplomatic Enclave , New Delhi. The following conditions may be carefully noted by 
institutions intending to make applications. 

(1 ) An application will not be considered from any institution , which has already 
received a grant for a period extending upto the 31st March , 1966 . 

( 2 ) Applications for starting now institutions in areas now included in a Welfare 
Extension Project will not be considered , except from institutions which have already 
existed in that area before the starting of that project . 

(3 ) Every ipstitution should give complete information about its management, 
that is , whether it is run by an individual or by Managing Committee elected 
or non -elected . Full details of existing assets and collections already made by volun . 
tary effort bbould be furnished . 

( 4 ) Every application should give brief details of the scheme for which the 
grant will be uptilised , as also the institution s normu) expenditure on those items and 
its matching contribution . 

In cases where the scheme is the maintenance of orphanago or a home for destitute 
wonen , etc. , or for the free distribution or milk or medicines , the number of existing 
iomates or beneficiaries and the additional number to be benefitted by grant should 
be clearly indicated . 

( 5 ) Branches of all India and regional organisations should be asked to send 
their applications to the Central Office of their organisation . The Central Office of 
the organisation should send the original application with its recommendation to the 
State Board and an advance copy for information to the Central Board , also with 
its recommendation , 
Note :-The statement of income and expenditure furnished by Branch should 

relate only to its owa income and expenditure, had not to the whole orga 
pisation . This applies also in cases where the same institution has a number 

of separate Branches in different places. 

(6 ) Since the grant will be only for a period of 6 six months, institutions should 
frame their , estimates for this period only and ask for only so much as they can 
spend by the end of March , 1956. No extention of the period will be granted 
subsequently . 

(7) A request for a gặant for each purpose should indicate the total ro 
quirements of the institution for the period in question for that purpose and the 
amount which will be met from its own resources . In tbe oase of requests for grants 
for new buildings, it should be indicated whether the institution has legal title to the 
land on wbich the building is príposed to be constructed . Similary , in the case of 
requests for grants for additions or alternations to buildings, it should be clearly indicated 
whether the institution has legal title to the land and existing building.

PRESS NOTE . 
INSTRUCTIONS TO EMPLOYEES TO DECLARE AUGUST 15 

A PAID HOLIDAY . 


In pursuance of instructions issued by the Central Ministry of Labour on pre 
vious anniversaries of Independence Day , Workers were permitted to participate in 
the August 15th celebrations without being made to suffer any lo88 in wages. 

A similar directive has been issued this year by the Govt. of India to their 
officers in charge of industrial undertakings and thay hope that other employers. 
also will co -operate with them by declaring this national day as a paid holiday . 

In view of the great importance of the occasion , Government believe that many 
industrial undertakings have already prescribed August 15th as one of the regular 
holidays but where this has not been done, they hope that the employers will tront 
the day an additional paid holiday and not as a substituted holiday.

Imphal, the 23rd August , 1986 . 
No. H. Apptt . 47 /55.- The following Notification No. 12 - Exam (18 ) /85 dt. 14-7-85 
received from the Registrar, the Institute Chartered Accountants of Iodia , Now 
Delhi- 1 , is published for general information : 

T. Kipgen 

Secretary to the Govt. of Manipur . 
In pursuance of Regulation 23 of the Chartered Accountants Regulations, 1949 , 
the Council of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India is pleased to direct 
that the Preliminary Examination under the said Regulations shall be held on the 
17th , 18th , 19th , 2ist and 22nd November 1953 , the First Examination on the 
17th , 18th , 19th , 21st, 22nd , 23rd and 2.4th November , 1965 and the Final Ex 
mination on the 17th 18th , 19th , 21st, 22nd , 23rd 

22nd , 23rd and 24th Nov. 1956. The 
examinations will be held at each of the following centres provided that a sufficient 
aumber of candidates present themselves for examination : 

(a ) ALLAHABAD , (b ) BOMBAY , ( c ) CALCUTTA , (d ) DELHI, (e ) HYDERABAD 
(Dn ) and (f ) MADRAS. 

Applications for admission to these examinations are required to be made on the 
prescribed forms, copies of which may be obtained from the Secretary to the Counoil 
of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India , New Delhi. Each such appli 
cation together with the necessary certificates and & Domand Draft payable at New 
Delhi and drawn in favour of the said Secretary for an examination fee of Rs . 25 / 
in the case of the Preliminary Examination , Rs . 50 /- in the of the First 
Examination and Rs . 75 /- for admission to both the Groups or Rs. 50 /- for admis 
sion to one group only of the Final Examination , must be sent so as to reach the

Imphal, the 29th August , 1955 . 
No. J/ 17 ;55 . -The following notification issued by the Central Government under 
Section 12 of the Commissions of Inquiry Act, 1952 is publishod for general infor 
mation : 

No. 16 / 1 / 55 - Judicial (I ) 

Government of India 
Ministry of Hom . Affairs. 

NOTIFICATION . 

New Delhi- 2 , the 26th July , 1956 . 
In exercise of the powers conferred by section 12 of the Commissions of Inquiry 
Act , 1952 (LX of 1952) , the Central Government hereby makes the following rules 
for the issue and service of summons by a Commission of Inquiry appointed by 
that Government, namely : 

Rules. 
1. The Commission may issue summons to persons whose attendance is 

required either to give evidence or to produce documents. 
Every summons issued by the Commission shall be in duplicate and 
signed by the Chairman or such person as he empowers in this behalf 
and sealed with the seal of the Commission ; and it shall specify the 
time and place at which the person summoned is required to attend 
and also whether his attendance is required for the purpose of giving 

evidence or to produce a document, or for both purposes. 
3 . A person may be summoned to produce a document, without being 

summoned to give evidence ; aud any person summoped merely to produce 
a docun : ent shall be deemed to have complied with the summons if 
he causes such document to be produced instead of attending personally 
to produce the same. 
A summons to produce documents may be for the produotion of certain 
specified documents or for the production of all documents of a certain 

description in the possession or power of the person summoned . 
6. Every summons shall be served by sending it by post to the person 

for whom it is intended or in such other manner as the Commission 


2 . 


may direct. 


6. The provisions of the foregoing rules shall apply , as far as may be, to 

Ovary other process issuod by the Commission . 


A. K. Bay , 
Chief Secretary to the Govt . of Manipur ,

PRESS NOTE 


CENTRAL STATES SCHOLARSHIPS -- 19 :56 . 


The Government of India offer to award in 1956-57 five scholarships to candi 
datos who by birth or domicilo are natives of Part C States or of Andamans 
and Nicobar Islands . 

The scholarships are tenable for three years or less depending upon the course 
of study choren and are intended for study or research in a foreign country in 
any branch of knowledge for which suitable facilities do not exist in India . Can . 
didates should not ordinarily be moro than 30 years of age on 1st January , 1956 . 

Application forms and the particulars can be obtained from the State Govern 
ment concerned . Completed application forms should reach the State Government 
concerncd not later than 15th October , 1955. All enquiries regarding the scholar 
ships should be addressed ouly to the State Government concerned . Applications 
received direct will not be considered .

PART II 
NOTIFICATION . 


Dated Shillong , the 5th September, 1955 . 


Subject : - Verification by the Treasury Officer of couutersignature on the Travel 

ling allowance claim of Gazetted Goveroment servant for the period 

prior to his transfer to the payment of a new Treasury Officer. 
No. TM./4/55/26.--A reference is invited to rule 177 of the Central Treasury 
Rule Vol-1, which inter -alia imposes an obligation on the Treasury Officer to verify 
the genuineness of the countersignature of the Controlling Officer on the Travel 
ling allowance claims of a gazetted Officer s bill . A question has been raised as to 
bow a Treasury Officer is to satisfy himself of the genuineness of the counter 
signature of the Controlling Officer in respect of a claim prior to the transfer of 
the officer to his payment . As the matter stands at present, no provision exists in 
the Treasury Rules providing for the action to be 

action to be taken by the now Treasury 
Officer in this regard . To meet this lacuna in the rules , it has been decided that 
all the controlling Officers empowered to countersign bills should sand their speci 
men signatures to all the Treasury Ollicers duly attested by the Treasury Officer 
of the district, in which they draw bills so that the new Treasury Officer may 
not have any difficulty to verify tho countersignature . 

The Controlling Officors (Central) and all the Treasury and Sub - Treasury Officers 
in Assam , Tripura and Manipur will please see that the procedure detailed above 
in this regard is strictly followed . 

Amitabha Ghosh , 
Doputy Accountant General ( II), Asgam .

MINISTRY OF INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING 

RESOLUTION 

New Delhi, the 2nd February 1955. 
: No. 1/51/54.F .-- Whereas the Film Advisory Board has been functioning for recom 
mending documentaries and newsreels produced by the Films Division und by private 
producers for grant of approval certificates with reforonce to the relevant condition in 
the cinema licences and whereas a direction bas now been issued by the Central Govern 
ment under sub- section (4 ) of section 12 of the Cinematogr4ph Act, 1952 (XXXVII of 
1952 ), and by the various State Governments under their own Acts , it has been decided 
that the Film Advisory Board should be entrusted with the responsibility of approving 
films which may be regarded as scientific films, films intended for educational purposes, 
films dealing with news and current events or documentary films with reference to these 
directions. 

2 . The rules governing the working of the Film Advisory Board will be as follows : 
( 1) The Board shall consist of not less than seven members , to be appointed by 
the Central Government , as follows : 

(a ) Chairman of the Central Board of Film ( ensors -- Ex -Officio Chairman . 
(b ) Regional Officer of the Central Board of Film Censors , Bombay - Esc 

Officio member. 
( c) A member of the Advisory Panel of the Central Board of Film Censors 

at Bombay 
(d) Not less than four other members including an educational and two 

persons with knowledge of films and film making . 


MANIPUR GAZETTE , OCTOBER 5 , 1955 . 


Explanation . — “ Regional Officer " includes “ Additional Regional Officer " und " Assistant 
Regional Officer ” . 


(2) Members other than the ex -officio members and the member of the Advisory 
Panel of the Central Board of Film Censors , Bombay , sbull be appointed for i period of 
two years and will be eligible for re- appointment. The member of the Advisory Panel 
sball be appointed as a member of the Board for the full term of his membership of the 
Panel. 


( 3 ) The Guvernment of India may for it cluse sufficient in its opinion , rem ve any 
momber of the Board before the expiration of the period of his office . 

( 4 ) Tbe non -official members of the Board will work in an honorary capacity . They 
may be paid such conpensatory allowance as the Central Government may from time 
to time determine . 


(6 ) The Regional Officer of the Central Board of Film Censors at Bombay will be 
the Secretary of the Board . 


(6 ) No act or proceeding of the Board shall be called in question on the ground 
merely of the existence of any Vacancy in or defect in the constitution of the Buard . 


(7 ) Unless otherwise directed by the Government of India , the Headquarters of the 
Board shall be at Bombay , 


(8 ) Meetings of the Board shall be presided over by the Chairman , and , in his 
absence the members present muy elect one among themselves to preside . 


( 9 ) The quorum of the Board shall be three . 


( 10 ) The decision of the Board shall be that of the majority of the members attend 
ing the meeting and in the event of an equality of votes, the presiding officer shall 
have a second or casting voto . The decision of thy Board shall be firal. If any appli 
cant wants to miiko any representation in regard to the film submitted by him , however , 
the Board shall give him an opportunity to do so and it shall be open to the Board 
to revise their decision in the light of any such representation . 

(11) The Board shall be ordinarily meet every week for the purpose of approving 
films as scientific filing , films intended for educational purposes , films dealing with 
news and ourrent events or doo:1tentary films in terms of th directions issued by the 
Government of India under sub -section (4 ) of section 12 of the Cinematograph Act , 1952 
(XXXVII of 195 :-) and any similar directions issued by the State Governments. 

( 12) Any person , firm , organisation or Government desirous of having any of his 
or its films approved by the Buard shall send an application in writing to the Secretary 
of the Board stating the title of the film and the source from which it can be obtained 
by the exhibitors ind such other particulars as may be rəquired by the Board . 

(13 ) The Board will communicate the titles and subje ate of the films approved by 
them , together with the informition reg irjing the sources from which they can be 
obtained , to the Contrul Governinent. The titles of the films certified to be scientific 
films, films intended for educational purposes, films dealing with news and current 
events or documentary films by thu Contral Government, with the approval of the film 
Advisory Buard , will be notifiod in the Gazette of India together with the address from 
which they can be obtained . 

P. M.LAD , Secy .

MINISTRY OF INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING 

RESOLUTION 

New Delhi, the 2nd February 1955 . 
No. 1 /51 /54.F. - Whereas the Film Advisory Board has been functioning for recom 
mending documentaries and newsreels produced by the Films Division and by private 
producers for grant of approval certificates with reference to the relevant condition in 
the oinema licences and whereas a direction has now been issued by the Central Govern 
ment under sub - section (4 ) of section 12 of the Cinematogruph Act, 1952 (XXXVII of 
1952), and by the various State Governments under their own Acts, it has been decided 
that the Film Advisory Board should be entrusted with the responsibility of approving 
films which may bo regarded as scientific films, films intended for educational purposes, 
films dealing with news and current events or documentary films with reference to these 
directions . 

2 . The rules governing the working of the Film Advisory Board will be az follows : 
( 1 ) The Board shall consist of not less than soven members , to be appointed by 
the Contral Government, as follows : 

(a ) Chairman of the Central Board of Film ( onsors— Ex -Officio Chairman . 
(b ) Regional Officer of the Central Board of Film Censors , Bombay - Ex 

Officio member . 
(c ) A member of the Advisory Panel of the Central Board of Film Censors 

at Bombay . 
(d ) Not less than four other members including an educational and two 

persons with knowledge of films and film making . 


MANIPUR GAZETTE , OCTOBER 5 , 1968. 


Explunation . - " Regional Officer” includes “ Additional Regional Officer" and " Assistant 
Regional Officer " . 


(2 ) Members other than the ex -officio members and the member of the Advisory 
Panel of the Central Board of Film Censors , Bombay, shull by appointed for a period of 
two years and will be eligible for re -appointment. The member of the Advisory Panel 
shall be appointed as a member of the Board for the full term of his membership of the 
Panel . 


( 3 ) The Guvernment of India may for it Oruse sufficient in its opinion , rem ve any 
murber of the Board bufore the expiration of the period of his office . 

(4 ) The non -ufficial members of the Board will work in an honorary c.ipacity . They 
may be paid such compensatory allowance as the Central Government may from time 
to time determina . 


(6 ) Tbe Regional Officer of the Central Board of Film Censors at Bombay will be 
the Secretary of the Board . 


(6 ) No act or proceeding of the Board shall be called in question on the ground 
merely of the existence of any Vacancy in or defect in the constitution of the Board . 


( 7 ) Unless otherwise directed by the Government of India , the Headquarters of the 
Board shall be at Bombay , 


(8 ) Meetings of the Board shall be presided over by the Chairman , and , in his 
absence the members present may elect one among themselves to preside . 


( 9 ) The quorum of the Board shall be three . 


( 10 ) The decision of the Board shall be that of the majority of the members attend 
ing the meeting and in the event of an equality of votes, the presiding officer shall 
have a second or casting vote. The decision of the Board shall be firal. If any appli 
cant wants to miiko any representation in regard to the film submitted by bin , however , 
the Board shall give him an opportunity to do so and it shall be open to the Board 
to revise their decision in the light of any such representation . 

(11 ) The Board shall be ordinarily meet every week for the purpose of approving 
films as scientific films, films intended for educational purposes , films dealing with 
news and current events or doc inentary films in terms of the directions issued by the 
Government of India under sub -section ( 4 ) of seciion 12 of the Cinematograph Act, 1962 
(XXXVII of 1952) and any similar directions issued by the State Governments. 

(12) Any person , firm , organisation or Government desirous of having any of his 
or its films approved by the Board shall send an application in writing to the Secretary 
of the Board stating the title of the film and the s jurc , from which it can be obtained 
by the exhibitors and such other particulars as may be raquired by the Board . 

(13) The Board will communicate the titles and subje sts of the films approved by 
them , together with the informition rogurling the sources from which they can be 
obtained , to the Central Government. The titles of the films certified to be scientific 
films, films intended for educational purposes , films dealing with news 

and current 
events or documentary films by the Central Government , with the approval of the film 
Advisory Board , will be notified in the Gazette of India together with the address from 
which they can be obtained . 

P. M.LAD , Secy .

Imphal, the 26th September, 1958 . 
With effect from the 28th September, 1953 , a daily courier service from Imphal 
to Tamenglong and vice versa will be set up to curry mails between these two head 
quarters . Lamboos of the Deputy Commissioner s establishment will work as couriers . 
The courier service will be open to 

utilisation by all Government Departments in 
Imphal as well as in Tamenglong . All mails intended for delivery to the S. D. O., 
Tamenglong or other Officers posted there should be lauded over to the Deputy Commis 
sioner s Office and those to be despatched from Tamenglong to Imphal by Officers 
there should be delivered to the Office of the S.D.O., Tamenglong for onward trans 
mission to the respective destinations. Mails should be banded over to the offices 
mentioned during office hours on working days and at 10 A.M. on holidays . 

Denartments concerned will please direct their messengers to the respoctive offices 
at Imphal and at Tamenglong every day to collect their mails . 
This arrangement will continue until further orders . 

V. 8 , SUNDARAM , 

Deputy Commissioner , Manipur .

NOTIFICATION . 

Dated Shillong, thi 1st Octoiser, 1955 . 
No. TM / 10 /55 / 31. - It is notified for informition and guidance of all Treasury 
Officers and Sub - lºreasury Officers in Assam , Tripura and Manipur that the remitters 
applications relative to drawings affected by the Treasuries and Sub- Treasuries do not in 
most cases contain the serial number and the actual date of issue of drafts . The absence 
of these essential particulars in the applications makes their identification with the relative 
paid drafts very difficult on the part of the Reserve Bank of India , Central Accounts 
Section , Calcutta . Consequently it gives rise to avoidable correspondence with the Drawing 
Officers . It is therefore , requested that all necessary particulars should invariably be 
furnished in the applications in the spuce provided for in the relative forms to avoid 
the difficulties so long experienced by the Riserve Bank of India . 

S. S. Lal, 
Deputy Accountant General ( I), Assam .
